answer_1.quote: Effective style transfer between these two text forms is crucial for applications such as education, crosscultural communication, and content localization.
answer_1.outputs: style-transferred texts (either from Singlish to English or vice versa)

answer_2.quote: The automatic metrics include: (1) Rank-based metrics (Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR) and HitRate@1 (HR@1)); (2) Content-based metrics (F1 and BLEU-1/2); and (3) Similarity-based metrics (BERTScore and BARTScore).

answer_3.quote: To evaluate these metrics, we leverage GPT-4 to rank the outputs of different methods according to their adherence to targeted style norms across specific linguistic aspects.

answer_4.quote: We engage three well-educated students and randomly sample 50 utterance pairs from the ExpCSEST dataset (i.e., outputs generated by our MACoE-Style and the baseline ICLEF). The evaluators are asked to indicate which utterance in each pair performs better by assigning 1 (WIN), 0 (TIE), or -1 (LOSE), considering the SC, CP, and FL perspectives, without exposing the source of the generated utterances.
answer_4.guideline: Evaluators compare pairs of outputs and assign WIN, TIE, or LOSE based on Style Control (SC), Content Preservation (CP), and Fluency (FL).
